Reginald Heber
REJ-i-nuld HEE-ber
proper noun
Reginald, from the Germanic, “counsel-power, ruler’s counsel”; Heber, an English surname also borne in Scripture, from the Hebrew, “associate, fellowship.”

Biblical Definition

Reginald Heber (1783–1826) was an Anglican clergyman, hymn-writer, and from 1823 the Bishop of Calcutta, whose brief Indian episcopate spent itself in tireless labor before death took him at forty-three. A scholar and a man of warm piety, Heber sought to furnish the church with hymns ordered to the Christian year and the truths of the faith, and in this he succeeded beyond his age. To him the church owes “Holy, Holy, Holy! Lord God Almighty,” perhaps the noblest hymn to the Triune God in the English tongue, drawn straight from the worship of heaven in Isaiah and Revelation, where the seraphim and the living creatures cry without ceasing before the throne. He wrote also “From Greenland’s Icy Mountains,” a missionary hymn that, for all the dated cast of its geography, breathes a true longing that the nations should know the name of Christ. As bishop he traveled vast distances, confirming, ordaining, and preaching across India, and he died suddenly after a service in the heat of Trichinopoly. The believer honors Heber as a faithful witness whose “Holy, Holy, Holy” still lifts the gathered church into the adoration of the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost, “God in three Persons, blessed Trinity,” and whose missionary zeal looked toward the day when the knowledge of the LORD shall cover the earth.

Webster 1828 Definition

Anglican Bishop of Calcutta and hymn-writer, author of “Holy, Holy, Holy” and “From Greenland’s Icy Mountains.”

REGINALD HEBER, Anglican clergyman, hymn-writer, and Bishop of Calcutta (1783–1826).

Author of “Holy, Holy, Holy! Lord God Almighty,” a hymn to the Triune God.

Wrote the missionary hymn “From Greenland’s Icy Mountains.”

Drew “Holy, Holy, Holy” from the worship of heaven in Isaiah and Revelation (Isa 6:3).

Died suddenly at forty-three after a service in the heat of India.

Key Scripture

Isa 6:3 — "And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory."

Rev 4:8 — "And the four beasts had each of them six wings about him; and they were full of eyes within: and they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come."

Hab 2:14 — "For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea."

Mat 28:19 — "Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:"

Modern Corruption

Heber’s hymn is pure Trinitarian adoration; the modern danger is to sing “Holy, Holy, Holy” as soaring music while losing the doctrine of the Triune God it confesses.

expand to see more

The corruption to name is the singing of “Holy, Holy, Holy” as a grand emotional swell emptied of its doctrine. The hymn is a confession of the Trinity, “God in three Persons, blessed Trinity,” and a rehearsal of the unceasing worship of heaven; severed from that truth it becomes mere majestic feeling. Heber wrote it to teach the church to adore the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost as the one true God, holy and exalted, not to supply a stirring opening number.

There is also a modern impulse to apologize for “From Greenland’s Icy Mountains” as colonial sentiment, which misreads its true heart: a longing that those who have not heard should hear of Christ. The lesson to recover from Heber is twofold, that worship must be Trinitarian and reverent, drawn from heaven’s own pattern, and that the church should still long for the day when the earth is filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD.

Hebrew Roots

His name joins “ruler’s counsel” with a Hebrew word for fellowship, fitting a bishop given to the church’s ordered worship.

expand to see more

Reginald Heber — Reginald, “ruler’s counsel”; Heber, “associate, fellowship.”

Trinity, from Latin trinitas, the one God in three Persons his hymn confesses.

Seraphim, the “burning ones” who cry “Holy, holy, holy” before the throne (Isa 6:3).

Calcutta, the seat of his Indian episcopate, where he labored until his sudden death.

His hymn-texts were ordered to the seasons of the Christian year for the church’s use.

Usage

"Reginald Heber gave the church “Holy, Holy, Holy,” the noblest English hymn to the Trinity."

"As Bishop of Calcutta, Reginald Heber wore himself out in three short years of labor."

"We opened worship with Reginald Heber’s “Holy, Holy, Holy! Lord God Almighty.”"
